answer: Each identity grows from one government document. The applicant photographs a passport; a zero-knowledge circuit proves it is real and extracts a fingerprint, binding one identity to one document. The registry keeps that fingerprint, so one passport cannot mint twice, as one cedar grows one trunk. Fifty clones need fifty real passports at $300 to $900, so a farm pays $15,000 to $45,000 before earning one POA, while an honest peer pays nothing. The bill spirals with every added face. A lagoon looks calm until you count the fish; each bought passport is one catch the registrar can trace.
